name: acquisition tracking standard
scope: Meta ad -> funnel (portal / quiz / presell / offer / checkout / upsells / receipt) -> purchase. Storefronts are not covered yet.

ad_url.why: Every Meta ad carries these URL tags (Meta's 'URL parameters' field, url_tags in the API). The funnel's attribution collector keeps utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content and sub1..sub5 on the Next Commerce cart and order; ad_id is read by the browser layer and Clarity. sub1 repeats the ad id because Next keeps sub1 and drops ad_id.
ad_url.never_in_the_link: The tags go in url_tags, not typed into the website URL: Meta does not fill {{...}} placeholders typed into the link of some formats, so the order arrives with the literal text {{ad.name}}.

email_url.why: Email links land in the same shape as ads, so one view can follow ad -> funnel -> purchase -> email -> repeat order. Set these in Klaviyo's UTM tracking (account, flow or campaign level).
email_url.content_section: utm_content is the message name, then '.' and the link's place in the email (button, logo, hero ...), so one email's links can be told apart: <message>.<section>. A campaign's message name is its send label.
email_url.funnel_why: A link to a CPK funnel page (a host and path a brand's tracking.json lists) also carries funnel=<that funnel's name>, the same value the page's browser layer puts on every event.
email_url.redirect_why: A coupon link is a redirect: the store's /discount/<code>/?next=<page> applies the code, then sends the reader to <page> with only <page>'s own query string, so tags on the outer link never reach the page (seen on Brand B.com, 2026-10-22). Such a link carries the tags on its target as well, URL-encoded inside next=, and the check asks for them there.
email_url.never_tagged: mailto:, tel:, sms:, '#' anchors, Klaviyo merge-tag links ({% ... %} / {{ ... }} as the whole link), unsubscribe and preference links, and links to sites that are not the brand's own (a partner's link keeps its own tracking).
email_url.klaviyo_why: Klaviyo's own UTM tracking (campaign tracking_options) is set to the same values for these keys, so whether Klaviyo or the link supplies a tag, the value is the same. utm_content stays on the link because it differs per link.
email_url.page_params: funnel, page and step are added by the page itself (the browser layer), the same as for ads
email_url.state: applied by the email line (components/email-production) since 2026-10-12: every own link in a built email carries these tags, Klaviyo drafts carry the same values in tracking_options, and the delivery gate holds an email whose own links miss them

attribution_params.why: Carried on every browser event (Meta custom data, GA4 event params, Clarity tags) so any event can be split by ad without opening Ads Manager.

params.brief: brief-NNNN parsed from the ad name
params.batch: batch-YYYY-MM-DD-x parsed from the ad name
params.page: the page's own name (last part of its path)
params.step: the step type of this page or screen (see events)

events.when: each quiz or portal screen shown; n is the 1-based screen number, step_name its id
the quiz or portal is finished (qualified / results shown)
the offer page loads (a product page whose next step is checkout)
a package goes into the cart
the checkout page loads with a cart

events.event_id: <store>-<order number>, the same id the Next Meta app sends server-side, so Meta keeps one

events.when: an upsell is accepted and charged (one order line)

step_types.why: How a page is classed when it has no explicit step. The layer derives it from the page's type and where it sends the visitor next.
rules: a page that mounts a portal or a quiz
a product page whose next step is not checkout
a product page whose next step is checkout

checker.note: checkout_start, payment_info, purchase and upsell_take need a cart or a real order; the checker loads pages only and never places an order, so it reports those as 'needs a test order'.
